LESSON: EFFECTIVE

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: Story Telling By the end of the sub-strand,  Learners listen to stories and mod
Topic 1.3: Effective

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Effective. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use compound and complex whole class talking to has SPEAKING sentences to link thoughts  Learners participate in play both in understood our
2. listen to concerns and opinions  Learners share their opinions and of others and represent them in represent the views of others to an appropriate forum relevant authorities e.g. child abuse
3. demonstrate willingness to interact with others
4. appreciate the importance of sharing one another’s feelings

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: EFFECTIVE
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 3
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Effective helps you succeed in LITERACY ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: EFFECTIVE
Study Effective like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Use compound and complex whole class talking to has SPEAKING sentences to link thoughts  Learners participate in play both in understood our

What this means
In this part you learn to use compound and complex whole class talking to has SPEAKING sentences to link thoughts  Learners participate in play both in understood our. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use compound and complex whole class talking to has SPEAKING sentences to link thoughts  Learners participate in play both in understood our.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use compound and complex whole class talking to has SPEAKING sentences to link thoughts  Learners participate in play both in understood our. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Demonstrate willingness to interact with others

What this means
In this part you learn to demonstrate willingness to interact with others. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: demonstrate willingness to interact with others.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model

Your turn

PART 4: Appreciate the importance of sharing one another’s feelings

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of sharing one another’s feelings. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of sharing one another’s feelings.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of sharing one another’s feelings. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Effective is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Effective”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: use compound and complex whole class talking to has SPEAKING sentences to link thoughts  Learners participate in play both in understood our)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Effective to a partner. (skill: listen to concerns and opinions  Learners share their opinions and of others and represent them in represent the views of others to an appropriate forum relevant authorities e.g. child abuse)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: demonstrate willingness to interact with others)

Example 4: Read a short paragraph about “Effective”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: appreciate the importance of sharing one another’s feelings)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Effective to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use compound and complex whole class talking to has SPEAKING sentences to link thoughts  Learners participate in play both in understood our.
3. Practise this skill: listen to concerns and opinions  Learners share their opinions and of others and represent them in represent the views of others to an appropriate forum relevant authorities e.g. child abuse.
4. Practise this skill: demonstrate willingness to interact with others.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Effective from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Effective: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 3 learner study Effective?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Effective means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use compound and complex whole class talking to has SPEAKING sentences to link thoughts  Learners participate in play both in understood our.
5. Be able to: listen to concerns and opinions  Learners share their opinions and of others and represent them in represent the views of others to an appropriate forum relevant authorities e.g. child abuse.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
